speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) whether the recent rise in rental prices of commercial properties have affected Singapore’s competitiveness and attractiveness as a business destination of choice; and (b) whether more can be done to moderate further rental increases.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In the same period, the vacancy rate for office spaces has remained stable at around 11% to 13%.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Rental continues to comprise a modest proportion of overall business costs for most sectors in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Government will continue to monitor the market.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We are committed to ensuring Singapore’s competitiveness and attractiveness as a business destination.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: In particular, can she elaborate on the 530,000 square metres of office space that are in the pipleline?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Where will this space be located and what kind of businesses would they cater for?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The second question is: the Minister of State mentioned in her reply that rentals form a modest proportion of the business costs for most sectors.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I think, to some, it is still quite significant.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Can I ask how would the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) ensure that Singapore remains overall competitive to be able to attract investments to Singapore with a rental that is reasonable and affordable to those companies?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: If I heard correctly, there are two parts to the first one.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I also wish him a speedy recovery after his ankle operation.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank him and assure him that the Government keeps a close eye on the cost of doing business and the impact on the economy as well as the impact on Singapore's attractiveness as a business location.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: To the first part of his first supplementary question, that is, to moderate the commercial rental prices, Mr Liang and Members will know that the Government has, in the past, implemented various supply-side measures, for example, calibrating sufficient supply to meet longer-term demand through the Government Land Sales (GLS) programme.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In addition, a 30-year lease commercial site in Punggol, potentially yielding about 8,400 square metres of office space as well as a mixed-use site in Woodlands, about 78,000 square metres of commercial space were also made available on the reserve list via the first half of 2023 GLS.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I cite all these examples to share and give assurance to the Member that these sites can be triggered by the developers to cater for additional commercial space demands.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And, of course, another important data to look at is the vacancy rate and I cited the figures of 11% to 13%.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: If I hear correctly, the second part of the Member's first question is about whether I can give some breakdown to the 530,000 square metres.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And to cater to companies in different sectors with different locational preferences, new office spaces will be distributed geographically across the island.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In the city fringe, that includes the Keppel South Central project that will be completed sometime next year and yield about 57,000 square metres.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Outside the CBD area, Punggol Digital District is expected to have an additional 39,000 square metres two years later in 2025.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: As other examples, next year, we will see completion of Labrador Tower, 75,000 square metres; next year as well, Paya Lebar Green, 36,000 square metres.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: To the Member's second question about Singapore's overall competitiveness, he would have read some of the recent ranking reports, including the Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU).

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: But we should not rest on our laurels.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: More importantly, I think the point here is that Singapore does not compete on cost alone.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Other factors that contribute to our city state's overall competitiveness include a stable political regime, strong rule of law, favourable policy towards foreign investment and trade, good digital and logistic connectivity, a skilled workforce as well as our technological infrastructure.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: But I want to reassure Mr Liang and all Members that the Government will certainly continue to monitor the market closely and, where needed, calibrate the supply of commercial properties to ensure the stability as well as the sustainability of rentals for business over the medium to long term.
